title: Robustness of the EFC Growth-Sector Signal: Leave-One-Out, Sound-Horizon, and Amplitude-Prior Controls for the Hubble-Friction Channel
description: This paper performs a joint Bayesian fit of the EFC coupling α to 14 BAO distance points and 7 fσ8 growth-rate measurements in the Hubble-friction channel, finding α = −1.00 ± 0.46 (2.20σ). It subjects the signal to three robustness controls—sound-horizon variation (N1), σ8 prior sensitivity (N2), and leave-one-out tests over all seven fσ8 points (T7)—and shows the signal is distributed, stable, and not driven by calibration or a single datum.

efc_friedmann.description: Background-level EFC modification to the Friedmann equation with a single late-time coupling α and gate function T(a) that activates at low redshift (z ≲ 2) to leave early-time ΛCDM intact.

key_results.main_finding: A joint BAO+growth fit yields α = −1.00 ± 0.46 (2.20σ), robust to sound-horizon variation, σ8 prior choice, and 7/7 leave-one-out tests.
datasets_used: BAO (14 points: 6dFGS, SDSS MGS, BOSS DR12, eBOSS LRG/QSO/ELG, Ly-α)
Growth rate fσ8 (7 points: 6dFGS, SDSS MGS, BOSS DR12×3, VIPERS, FastSound)

sealed_predictions.statement: In the Hubble-friction channel, tighter external constraints on σ8 (e.g., from weak lensing) will maintain a non-positive α, with any combined BAO+fσ8+lensing analysis continuing to prefer α ≤ 0 if the hinted late-time growth suppression is real.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint DESI fσ8 + Stage-III/IV weak-lensing (S8) + BAO analysis yielding α > 0 at ≥ 3σ significance.

kill_criteria: KC1: Expanded BAO+RSD (e.g., DESI DR1/DR2) analysis with the same MVP-G1 pipeline and comparable priors returns α = 0 ± 0.20 (|α|/σ < 1) and ΔBIC ≥ 6 in favor of ΛCDM, eliminating the need for the α parameter.
KC2: Growth-only constraints with tight external priors on Ωm and σ8 (from CMB+lensing) find α ≥ 0 at ≥ 3σ, contradicting the EFC late-time growth-suppression prediction.

KC3: Sound-horizon robustness fails decisively: varying r_d within the Planck posterior shifts the best-fit α by |Δα| ≥ 0.3 or flips its sign in high-precision datasets, indicating calibration dependence incompatible with the EFC formulation.

KC4: Leave-one-out and survey-split tests on an expanded (N ≥ 20) fσ8 set show instability—multiple removals yield |α|/σ < 1.0 or sign flips—with ΔAIC ≥ 0 overall, indicating the signal was a single-survey/systematics artefact.

KC5: Independent probes of late-time growth (e.g., ISW tomography or weak-lensing cosmic shear) jointly constrain the EFC parameter to α = 0 ± 0.15 with ΔBIC ≥ 6 favoring ΛCDM across cross-correlated datasets.
abstract_short: Joint Bayesian fit to 14 BAO + 7 fσ₈ points yields α = −1.00 ± 0.46 (2.20σ). Three robustness controls pass: sound-horizon independence (N1), amplitude-prior control (N2), leave-one-out 7/7 (T7). Signal is distributed, robust, sub-detection-threshold hint for late-time growth suppression.

N1_sound_horizon.description: Vary r_d within Planck posterior range

N2_amplitude_prior.description: Tight σ₈ prior vs flat prior

T7_leave_one_out.description: Remove each fσ₈ point and refit

degeneracy_structure.interpretation: Positive r(α,Ω_m): geometric degeneracy. Negative r(α,σ₈): growth suppression trades off against lower σ₈.

caveats: ΔBIC = −0.91: Bayesian penalty nearly cancels χ² improvement
Data consistent with α ≠ 0 but do not demand it

key_conclusions: ~2σ preference for α < 0 (late-time growth suppression) is NOT driven by sound-horizon calibration
Signal is NOT an artefact of σ₈ prior width
Signal is NOT carried by any single fσ₈ measurement
Signal distributed across full redshift range z = 0.02–0.85
Robust sub-detection-threshold hint awaiting confirmation by forthcoming surveys
